description:
Sibling propagation of the fix from bd:JMAP-1rwf.2 (the calendars-types alias).

Two type crates carry the same anti-pattern:

  - crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/lib.rs:45 — 'pub use jmap_jscalendar_types as jscalendar;'
  - crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/lib.rs:114 — 'pub use jmap_jscontact_types as jscontact;'

Both re-export the entire upstream crate under a nested module path that consumers may import via (e.g. 'jmap_tasks_types::jscalendar::*' or 'jmap_contacts_types::jscontact::*'). Any future addition to jmap-jscalendar-types or jmap-jscontact-types silently widens these crates' public surfaces without an intentional decision.

Apply the same fix landed at bd:JMAP-1rwf.2: replace the 'pub use X as Y;' alias with 'pub mod Y { pub use X::{... explicit list ...}; }' where the explicit list is exactly the names already in the top-level re-export below (line ~60 in each crate). The legacy nested path stays working; future additions to the upstream crate require an intentional decision in both the alias module and the top-level re-export.

This is not a canonical-template propagation (jmap-mail-types is the canonical for extension-types and has no equivalent JS* alias). It is a per-crate fix to the two crates that copied the calendars-types pattern.

Acceptance:
  - crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/lib.rs: 'pub use jmap_jscalendar_types as jscalendar' replaced with explicit re-export module.
  - crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/lib.rs: 'pub use jmap_jscontact_types as jscontact' replaced with explicit re-export module.
  - Workspace cargo test green, cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings green, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc green.
  - No public-API break: existing 'jmap_tasks_types::jscalendar::Location' and 'jmap_contacts_types::jscontact::Name' paths still resolve.
title: tasks-types + contacts-types: same uncontrolled-public-surface alias pattern as calendars-types
